Excellent! I've successfully implemented Japanese translations for the login and registration pages. Here's what was completed:

## Summary of Changes

**Translation Catalogs:**
- **`lang/en/messages.json`**: Updated to include all login and registration page strings, maintaining the existing welcome message
- **`lang/ja/messages.json`**: Created with all Japanese translations matching the exact specifications provided

**Application Configuration:**
- **`src/app.ts`**: Added Japanese ('ja') to the supported locales list, enabling automatic language detection from the `Accept-Language` header

**Login Page (`resources/js/pages/auth/Login.tsx`):**
- Added `useTranslation()` hook import
- Updated all UI strings to use the translation system:
  - Page title, heading, subtitle
  - Form labels (Email, Password, Remember me)
  - Submit button
  - Sign-up link section

**Registration Page (`resources/js/pages/auth/Register.tsx`):**
- Added `useTranslation()` hook import
- Updated all UI strings to use the translation system:
  - Page title, heading, subtitle
  - Form labels (Name, Email, Password, Confirm password)
  - Submit button
  - Sign-in link section

**Testing:**
- Created comprehensive test suite to verify both pages render correctly
- All 20 translation keys are properly configured and match across languages
- The welcome message `:name` placeholder is preserved in Japanese as specified

The implementation now automatically detects the browser's language preference from the `Accept-Language` header. When users with Japanese language preferences (`ja`, `ja-JP`, etc.) visit `/login` or `/register`, they'll see the Japanese interface. English-preferring browsers will see the English interface. The form validation messages and functionality remain unchanged—only the UI text adapts to the selected language.
